newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate up to 12.2 vs 11.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate up to 12.2 vs 11.6 pct.

text.p: Continued shortage of kuna funds pushed Croatia's average lending rate further up to 12.2 percent from 11.6 percent on Monday, dealers said.
They put the total daily trade at 79.7 million kuna, of which 73.1 million were fresh borrowings. Borrowers' demand for further 8.3 million kuna could not be met.
The weighted call money rate rose to 11.6 percent from 10.5 percent on Friday.
Insurers rolled over previous loans at 9 percent and term loans were struck at 14 and 15 percent.
Croatia's Bank for Development and Reconstruction granted a 30 million kuna loan to ailing Privredna Banka, which is to be overhauled soon, at a call money rate of 12 percent.

The Central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Tuesday slightly firmer at 5.5231 against the dollar and weaker at 3.5573 against the German mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
